title: Derived reduction of an extension by a divisible sheaf
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with a final object, and let $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $R=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], where $n\geq1$. Work in sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their cohomological derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $B,F$ be abelian sheaves such that $n:B\to B$ is an epimorphism and $n:F\to F$ is a monomorphism. Put $H=\ker(n:B\to B)$, with its natural $R$-module structure, and $\bar F=\operatorname{coker}(n:F\to F)$. Let $S$ be a short exact sequence $0\to B\to M\to F\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], with connecting morphism $\partial_S:F\to B[1]$, the last arrow of its derived short-exact-sequence triangle [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. For the derived change of rings $Lq=-\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}}R$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], there are natural identifications in $D(R)$
$$Lq(F)\simeq\bar F[0],\qquad Lq(B)\simeq H[1].$$
Normalize the second identification so that the scalar-extension unit $B\to\operatorname{Res}Lq(B)\simeq H[1]$ is the connecting morphism $\kappa_B$ of $0\to H\to B\xrightarrow{n}B\to0$. Thus $Lq(\partial_S)$ defines a canonical morphism $d_{S,n}:\bar F\to H[2]$ of $D(R)$. For every sheaf map $s:\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to F$, let $\bar s:R\to\bar F$ be its reduction. Under the derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], the morphism $d_{S,n}\bar s:R\to H[2]$ corresponds to
$$\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{s}F\xrightarrow{\partial_S}B[1]\xrightarrow{\kappa_B[1]}H[2]$$
in $D(\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C})$; in particular it is the Kummer-type connecting image of the extension boundary of $s$. These identifications and morphisms are natural for morphisms of short exact sequences satisfying these hypotheses and for exact inverse-image functors of geometric morphisms of topoi (left adjoints preserving finite limits), with the induced constant-ring identifications. Here $\operatorname{Res}$ is termwise restriction of scalars, and the adjunction has unit induced by $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to R$.

proof.text: Put $Z=\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and let $E=-\otimes_Z R$ on sheaves. Apply the module adjunction to the identity morphism of the topos with ring map $Z\to R$: $E\dashv\operatorname{Res}$. Restriction keeps the underlying abelian sheaf; the sectionwise kernel and sheafified cokernel formulas therefore show that it is exact. The exact-functor results identify its everywhere-defined right derived functor with termwise restriction. Derived change of rings gives the everywhere-defined $LE=Lq$, so the derived-adjoint-functors theorem gives $Lq\dashv\operatorname{Res}$. Its unit $\eta$ is the derived ordinary unit: on a K-flat complex $P$, under $Lq(P)\simeq E(P)$, it is $P\to\operatorname{Res}E(P)$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Indeed, in the pre-derived adjunction formula take the target complex to be $E(P)$, its restriction resolution to be the identity, and the map $P\to\operatorname{Res}E(P)$ to be the ordinary unit; its ordinary adjunct is $\mathrm{id}_{E(P)}$. The formula then says that its derived adjunct is also the identity. The termwise unit commutes with shifts: the maps in each degree are unchanged and both shifted differentials acquire the same sign. For a resolution $P\to A$, use $P[k]\to A[k]$ to compute the shifted object; its scalar extension is $(P\otimes_Z R)[k]$, and its unit is the shift of the unit on $P$. Under the canonical resolution isomorphisms this proves $\eta_{A[k]}=\eta_A[k]$, with the shift isomorphisms of $Lq$ and restriction understood.

source.place: Paragraphs 4–5, scalar extension and the adjunction used to interpret its boundary; Stacks Tags 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors) and 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general) supply the general tools.

proof.text: The sequence $0\to Z\xrightarrow{n}Z\to R\to0$ is exact as a sequence of sheaves: a section of a constant sheaf is locally an integer (respectively a residue class), integer multiplication by $n\ge1$ is injective, and residue classes lift locally to integers. For any $Z$-module sheaf $A$, there is a natural isomorphism $A\otimes_Z R\simeq A/nA$. The mutually inverse local formulas are $a\otimes\bar k\mapsto ka\bmod nA$ and $a\bmod nA\mapsto a\otimes\bar1$. Changing a lift $k$ by $n\ell$ changes the first expression by $n\ell a$, and $na\otimes\bar1=a\otimes\bar n=0$ makes the second well defined; sheafification glues these local formulas. Here $A/nA$ is the sheaf cokernel, not necessarily the quotient of global sections.

source.place: Paragraph 4, explicit ordinary reduction underlying the derived reduction; elementary calculation with constant sheaves and the tensor product.

proof.text:
For an abelian sheaf $A$, choose a K-flat resolution $p:P\to A[0]$ whose terms are flat. Set $Q_A=P\otimes_Z R=P/nP$, an actual complex of $R$-modules representing $Lq(A)$. Tensoring the exact coefficient sequence of step 2 with each flat term $P^j$ preserves exactness by the definition of flatness. Thus $0\to P\xrightarrow{n}P\to\operatorname{Res}Q_A\to0$ is degreewise short exact. Let $j:P\to\operatorname{Res}Q_A$ be the quotient, $\partial_P:\operatorname{Res}Q_A\to P[1]$ its short-exact-sequence boundary, and $c_A:Lq(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A$ the canonical resolution isomorphism. Apply $p,p,\operatorname{Res}(c_A)^{-1}$ to the three vertices of the short-exact-sequence triangle. This gives the distinguished triangle
$$A\xrightarrow{n}A\xrightarrow{\eta_A}\operatorname{Res}Lq(A)\xrightarrow{\delta_A}A[1].$$
Here $\delta_A=p[1]\circ\partial_P\circ\operatorname{Res}(c_A)$, and the middle arrow is $\operatorname{Res}(c_A)^{-1}\circ j\circ p^{-1}=\eta_A$ by naturality of the unit and its formula on $P$ in step 1. This uses a K-flat resolution of the input $A$, so $Q_A$ retains its $R$-module structure.

source.place: Paragraph 4, derived reduction computed using flat-term K-flat input resolutions; Stacks Tags 06YS, 06YU and 0152.

proof.text:
Apply the cohomology long exact sequence to the triangle in step 3 and to its rotation $A\xrightarrow{\eta_A}\operatorname{Res}Lq(A)\xrightarrow{\delta_A}A[1]\xrightarrow{-n[1]}A[1]$ (TR2 of the triangulated-category definition); exactness of the long sequence of the rotated triangle at its third vertex shows that the map $H^{-1}(\operatorname{Res}Q_A)\to H^{-1}(A[1])=A$ in the sequence below is $H^{-1}(\delta_A)$. Since $A[0]$ has cohomology only in degree zero, it gives
$$H^j(Q_A)=0\quad(j\ne-1,0),\qquad
0\to H^{-1}(\operatorname{Res}Q_A)\xrightarrow{H^{-1}(\delta_A)}A\xrightarrow{n}A\xrightarrow{H^0(\eta_A)}H^0(\operatorname{Res}Q_A)\to0.$$
Restriction is exact, so these are the underlying abelian sheaves of the $R$-cohomology sheaves of $Q_A$. For $A=F$, injectivity of $n$ kills $H^{-1}$ and gives the canonical quotient isomorphism $H^0(Q_F)\simeq\bar F$. For $A=B$, epimorphy of $n$ kills $H^0$ and identifies $H^{-1}(Q_B)$ with $H$ as an abelian sheaf. Every map between abelian sheaves annihilated by $n$ is automatically $R$-linear: locally a scalar is an integer modulo $n$, and an additive map commutes with integer multiplication.

source.place: Paragraph 4, the quotient and torsion cohomology calculations. The precise sign of the target identification is fixed in step 6.

proof.text:
For any complex $Q$ of $R$-modules with cohomology only in degree $a$, the canonical zigzag
$$Q\ \longleftarrow\ \tau_{\le a}Q\ \longrightarrow\ H^a(Q)[-a]$$
consists of quasi-isomorphisms in complexes of $R$-modules. Explicitly, the left arrow includes the complex with term $\ker(d^a)$ in degree $a$ and zero above $a$; the right arrow is zero below $a$ and the quotient $\ker(d^a)\to\ker(d^a)/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})$ in degree $a$. Both arrows induce the identity on the sole nonzero cohomology. The definitions of truncation and localization therefore give a natural isomorphism in $D(R)$, not merely after restriction. With $a=0$ this gives $\alpha_F:Lq(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar F[0]$ using step 4. With $a=-1$ it identifies $Lq(B)$ with $H^{-1}(Q_B)[1]$; step 6 chooses the isomorphism of that cohomology sheaf with $H$ required by the normalization.

source.place: Paragraph 4, passage from the computed cohomology sheaves to actual identifications in the coefficient derived category.

proof.text:
Let $i:H\hookrightarrow B$. The Kummer short exact sequence $0\to H\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{n}B\to0$ gives its canonical triangle with boundary $\kappa_B$. Rotate it using the triangulated-category sign convention to obtain
$$B\xrightarrow{n}B\xrightarrow{\kappa_B}H[1]\xrightarrow{-i[1]}B[1].$$
Compare this triangle to step 3 for $A=B$, using identities on the first two copies of $B$. Axiom TR3 supplies $t:\operatorname{Res}Lq(B)\to H[1]$ satisfying
$$t\eta_B=\kappa_B,\qquad (-i[1])t=\delta_B.$$
Taking degree $-1$ shows that $H^{-1}(t)$ is an isomorphism: both $-i$ and $H^{-1}(\delta_B)$ identify their sources with the kernel of $n:B\to B$. Moreover $H^{-1}(t)$ is uniquely determined by $(-i)H^{-1}(t)=H^{-1}(\delta_B)$ since $i$ is monic, and it is $R$-linear by step 4. Use this cohomology isomorphism in the $R$-linear zigzag of step 5 to define $\alpha_B:Lq(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}H[1]$ in $D(R)$. The restriction of $\alpha_B$ equals $t$: their maps on degree $-1$ cohomology agree, and after the single-cohomology identifications the shifted single-complex fully-faithfulness theorem says such maps are determined by that cohomology map. Consequently $(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)\eta_B=\kappa_B$, with the sign fixed by the displayed rotated triangle.

source.place: Paragraph 4, normalization by the Kummer boundary; Stacks Tags 0152, 0145 (rotation and TR3), and 06XS (single-complex fully faithfulness).

proof.text: For a map of extensions f and compatible maps h:H→H' and q:Fbar→Fbar', prove the two normalized identification squares by injectivity of the derived scalar adjunction's Hom equivalence. For alphaF, the adjuncts agree after the invertible single/restriction comparison: naturality of eta and the quotient-unit equations reduce this to f_3 followed by p' equals p followed by Res(q). For alphaB, naturality of eta and the Kummer-unit equations reduce the adjuncts to f_1 followed by kappa' equals kappa followed by Res(h[1]). The latter is naturality of the canonical single short-exact triangle for the map of Kummer sequences with components Res(h), f_1, f_1, followed by naturality of the single/restriction and shift comparisons. Thus no simultaneous K-flat diagram replacement is needed: the normalization equations already determine all the relevant morphisms by the adjunction.

source.place: Paragraphs 4–5, functoriality of the normalized reduction identifications; finite arrow diagrams meet the smallness hypotheses.

proof.text:
Apply the functorial complex short-exact-sequence triangle to $S$ concentrated in degree zero. Its boundary is $\partial_S:F\to B[1]$, natural for maps of such sequences. It is the boundary of the statement: if $\delta'$ is any morphism making $B\to M\xrightarrow{g}F\xrightarrow{\delta'}B[1]$ distinguished as in the derived short-exact-sequence triangle, TR3 applied to the identities of $B$ and $M$ gives $c:F[0]\to F[0]$ with $cg=g$ and $\partial_S=\delta'c$; by single-complex fully faithfulness $c$ is a sheaf endomorphism, and $g$ is an epimorphism, so $c=\mathrm{id}$ and $\delta'=\partial_S$. The same argument shows that $\kappa_B$ of step 6 is the unique boundary of the Kummer sequence. Derived scalar extension is exact and commutes with shifts, so define in $D(R)$
$$d_{S,n}=\alpha_B[1]\circ Lq(\partial_S)\circ\alpha_F^{-1}:\bar F[0]\to H[2].$$
The functoriality of the boundary together with step 7 proves naturality of $d_{S,n}$ for maps of extensions.

source.place: Paragraph 4, apply derived reduction to the Cartier extension boundary.

proof.text:
The complex $Z[0]$ is K-flat because tensoring any complex with it is the identity; hence $Lq(Z)=R[0]$. The cohomology quotient calculation of steps 2–5 shows that $\alpha_F Lq(s):R[0]\to\bar F[0]$ is $\bar s$: in degree zero it sends the local residue class of an integer $k$ to the class of $s(k)$. Single-complex fully faithfulness identifies the derived morphism with this sheaf map. By the unit formula for an adjunction, naturality of $\eta$ for $s$ and for the derived morphism $\partial_S$, and the shift compatibility in step 1, the adjunct of $d_{S,n}\bar s$ equals
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Res}(d_{S,n}\bar s)\eta_Z
&=(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)[1]\,\operatorname{Res}Lq(\partial_S)\,\operatorname{Res}Lq(s)\,\eta_Z\\
&=(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)[1]\,\operatorname{Res}Lq(\partial_S)\,\eta_F s\\
&=\bigl((\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)\eta_B\bigr)[1]\,\partial_S s
=\kappa_B[1]\,\partial_S s.
\end{aligned}$$
The cancellations in the first line use $\bar s=\alpha_F Lq(s)$ and the definition of $d_{S,n}$. The last equality is exactly the normalization proved in step 6.

source.place: Paragraph 5, identify the composite with the Kummer connecting image; Stacks Tags 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors), 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors) and 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general) provide the natural adjunction.

proof.text:
Finally let $u^{-1}$ be an exact inverse-image functor as in the statement. Since it is a left adjoint preserving finite limits, it preserves the constant rings: a constant object is the coproduct of copies of the final object, and it preserves this coproduct and the final object. Exactness preserves $\ker n$, $\operatorname{coker}n$ and both short exact sequences, including the injectivity/epimorphy hypotheses. The ringed-topoi tensor-pullback theorem says that $u^{-1}P$ is again flat-term K-flat, so the exactness of $u^{-1}$ makes it a resolution of $u^{-1}A$. Its scalar-reduction complex is
$$u^{-1}(P/nP)=(u^{-1}P)/n(u^{-1}P).$$
Indeed exactness preserves the cokernel and the tensor-pullback comparison identifies the two scalar-extension models. The termwise units $P\to P/nP$ are preserved by this equality. The exact-functor factorization gives the termwise triangulated action on derived categories. Explicitly, for a short exact sequence $0\to X\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{b}T\to0$, let $q:C(a)\to T$ be $b$ on the $Y$ summand and zero on $X[1]$, and let $p:C(a)\to X[1]$ be the projection; its canonical boundary is $-p\circ q^{-1}$ (Stacks Tag 0152, label lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor). Additivity identifies $u^{-1}C(a)$ with $C(u^{-1}a)$, with exactly the same differential matrix, and sends $q,p$ to the corresponding maps $q',p'$. Exactness makes $u^{-1}q$ a quasi-isomorphism, so applying $u^{-1}$ to the boundary gives $-p'\circ(q')^{-1}$, the boundary of the pulled-back sequence. It also commutes with the truncation zigzags because it preserves kernels and images. The equation $(-i)H^{-1}(t)=H^{-1}(\delta_B)$ is consequently preserved, so uniqueness in step 6 preserves the normalized $\alpha_B$ as well. Thus $\alpha_F$, $\alpha_B$, $d_{S,n}$ and the displayed adjunct formula all commute with $u^{-1}$ under the induced constant-ring identifications.

split_report.summary: Split into ten steps using flat-term K-flat resolutions of the input, the multiplication triangle, cohomology and R-linear truncation zigzags. Fix the target sign by comparison with the rotated Kummer triangle, then calculate the adjunct and prove both naturality clauses. No new nodes; statement unchanged. The initial draft was strengthened to avoid treating a restricted two-term complex as an R-complex. Second reading expands the resolution comparison arrows, unit shift compatibility and inverse-image boundary formula; the statement and dependency set remain unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Step 3 uses arbitrary-site flat-term K-flat resolutions; this is generic derived-category machinery, not a substitute for a Cartier unit step.
Steps 1, 3, 7–9 use the everywhere-defined exact K-flat scalar-extension functor; this is the scalar-extension machinery required by the Cartier route.
Step 1 specializes the module pullback/pushforward adjunction to the identity topos and Z→R; the Cartier unit does not prove this general module adjunction.
Steps 1 and 10 use the termwise triangulated functor of an exact functor, including shift compatibility, for restriction and inverse image.
Step 1 identifies exact restriction with its everywhere-defined right derived functor, needed to apply the derived-adjunction theorem.
Steps 1 and 9 use the general derived-adjunction theorem for everywhere-defined derived functors to obtain Lq left adjoint to termwise restriction.
Steps 1 and 9 use the fraction formula and derived-variable naturality to identify the unit with the termwise quotient on K-flat inputs.
Steps 3, 6–8 and 10 use the canonical boundary of a degreewise short exact sequence and its naturality; this is general derived homological algebra.
Step 4 uses the cohomology exact sequence of a distinguished triangle; the Cartier unit requires this generic calculation.
Steps 6, 7 and 9 use fully faithfulness of single sheaves in the derived category to compare morphisms between single-cohomology objects.
Step 7 uses a simultaneous replacement of a finite arrow diagram to justify naturality of the multiplication triangles.
Step 10 uses preservation of flat-term K-flat resolutions and natural tensor comparison by a general ringed-topos inverse image.
